answer: A robust defense is verifiable work history bound to a stake: each agent builds a checkable record of completed tasks and peer attestations, and must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact. Like a lotus, trust grows slowly, one verified job at a time, while a spiral of fake identities gains nothing because every new identity starts with zero history and must post its own stake. To reach the zenith of reputation, an attacker would have to fund and operate many identities through real, costly work over a long period, which makes a large-scale Sybil attack economically irrational.
